reconstructed_theorem_text:
For every complete finite-dimensional real inner-product space E with its Borel measurable structure,consider a globally twice continuously Frechet differentiable f:E->R,real kappa,h and natural J. Assume kappa>=1,J>=2,h>0,and for all base points z and vectors v in E,
  (1/(2kappa))||v||^2 <= D^2 f(z)[v,v] <= ||v||^2.
For the actual indices i,j in Fin(J)={0,...,J-1},define exactly
  t_i=(h/2)(1-cos((i/(J-1))pi)),
  ell_j=the real Lagrange cardinal polynomial at these nodes,
  Lambda=sup{sum_j |ell_j(s)|:s in [0,h]},
  omega_ij=integral_0^{t_i}(t_i-s)ell_j(s)ds,
  b_j=integral_0^h ell_j(s)ds,
  c_j=integral_0^h(h-s)ell_j(s)ds.
The node quotient uses real coercions. The supremum is real,and the interval integrals are ordinary Lebesgue Bochner integrals. If
  h Lambda<=1/(65536kappa),
put a=exp(-h/2),sigma=sqrt(1-exp(-h)). For an incoming phase state z=(X,P) and supplied vector pair zeta=(u,v),define
  P0(z,zeta)=a P+sigma u,
  Y0_j(z,zeta)=X+t_j P0(z,zeta),
  Y1_i(z,zeta)=Y0_i(z,zeta)-sum_j omega_ij grad f(Y0_j(z,zeta)),
  Phi(z,zeta)=(X+h P0(z,zeta)-sum_j c_j grad f(Y1_j(z,zeta)),
               a(P0(z,zeta)-sum_j b_j grad f(Y1_j(z,zeta)))+sigma v).
The gradient is the actual Riesz representative of the first Frechet derivative of f. All sums range over the entire Fin(J) index set. Define the exact quadratic energy
  Q_kappa(x,p)=(1/(2kappa)+1/2)||x||^2+<x,p>+||p||^2.
Then for every z,zprime,zeta in E x E,letting deltaX=z.1-zprime.1 and deltaP=z.2-zprime.2,
  sqrt(Q_kappa((Phi(z,zeta).1-Phi(zprime,zeta).1)-deltaX,
               (Phi(z,zeta).2-Phi(zprime,zeta).2)-deltaP))
    <=12h sqrt(Q_kappa(deltaX,deltaP)).
Equivalently the pair inside Q on the left is the increment difference (Phi(z,zeta)-z)-(Phi(zprime,zeta)-zprime),with coordinatewise subtraction. The square roots are real nonnegative square roots;the energy has cross coefficient exactly 1. Both noise vectors are shared between the two compared updates. Quantification is pointwise over every supplied noise pair,with no probability distribution or almost-everywhere restriction.
The theorem asserts this exact bound on the difference of increments. It does not state a contraction factor for the full output difference,an absolute bound on an individual update increment,a probability-kernel or transport result,a sampling history,an evaluation-count bound,or a remainder-operator representation. No supplied positive-form or metric certificate is an additional hypothesis.
